content.title: About
content.content: Kung Pao Chicken is a classic Chinese dish featuring diced chicken breast stir‑fried with peanuts, dried chilies, vegetables, and a savory soy‑based sauce. It delivers a spicy‑sweet flavor profile and the distinctive aroma of Sichuan peppercorns.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in Sichuan province in the 19th century and was originally made with duck.
The name “Kung Pao” (宫保) comes from the title “Gongbao,” held by the Qing‑dynasty official Ding Baozhen.
Traditional recipes use dried red chilies, but the heat level can be adjusted to taste.
Peanuts add a crunchy contrast to the tender chicken pieces.
The classic sauce combines soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sugar for a balanced sweet‑savory taste.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides a complete source of high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Peanuts supply monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish offers niacin, vitamin B6, and other B‑vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Dried chilies and soy sauce contain antioxidants that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium, and zinc are present, contributing to immune function and metabolic processes.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds significant salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Spiciness of chilies
items.content: Dried chilies may irritate the gastrointestinal tract; those with sensitive stomachs should reduce the amount.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish is relatively calorie‑rich due to oil and nuts; moderation is advised for weight‑controlled diets.

content.title: How to Serve
content.content: Kung Pao Chicken is typically served hot with steamed rice or noodles. Garnish with fresh cilantro or sliced green onions and sprinkle extra peanuts for added crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat with a splash of oil to retain the peanuts’ crunch.
